reasons: Classic holding-company conversion via 물적분할: the listed parent renames itself DAESUNG HOLDINGS, adds 지주사업 to its charter, and moves its entire core city-gas business (99.2% of revenue, ~2/3 of assets) into an unlisted 100% subsidiary — a structure that in Korea frequently precedes an opco IPO to relieve the holdco discount and fund the holdco's investment arm.

The parent explicitly separates an '투자사업부문' (already ~1,300억 of non-subsidiary investments) with ambitions in alternative energy/overseas resources; the regulated gas opco is the group's cash cow, so partial monetization (IPO or minority investor) is the natural funding route, and listing would also lower the Fair Trade Act minimum holdco stake (unlisted 40% → listed 20%).

Structural hints of IPO-readiness: the newco's authorized shares (80,000,000) are 4x the issued 20,000,000, and the correction re-allocates 500억 of corporate bonds to the newco, leaving a debt-light holdco and a standalone, normally leveraged utility balance sheet.

Counterweights: a monopoly, government-tariffed utility with stable cash flow that 'self-funds easily' has little need for outside equity; the filing states the newco will be 비상장, recruits no other shareholders, and mentions no IPO, investor, or sale; family-controlled group may prefer full ownership.

A sale of majority control of the group's core business is very unlikely; the realistic disposal routes are a partial IPO or a minority strategic/PEF investment, keeping parent control. Base rates for 물적분할-based holdco conversions of a core business are mixed (some IPO/PEF entries within ~5 years, others retained), so the forecast sits near a coin flip.
